cyber_risk_snapshot.marketingCopy: Most small businesses don't know their biggest cyber risks - and the ones they worry about are often not the ones that actually keep owners up at night. The Cyber Risk Snapshot is a rapid, high-level security review that evaluates your business across identity, endpoints, email, backup, network, and physical security in a single engagement. We produce a numerical risk score, red/amber/green ratings per domain, and a short list of the five most critical actions you should take first. It's the fastest way to go from 'we should probably do something about security' to a concrete, prioritized plan - and it makes an ideal starting point before a deeper assessment or an insurance application.
bestFor: Business owners who want a quick, affordable overview of their real cyber risk
Organizations that have never had any security assessment and need a starting point
Companies preparing for their first cyber insurance application
Businesses that want to identify and fix the most critical risks before the rest
whatIsIncluded: High-level security posture review across six domains
Numerical risk score with per-domain red, amber, and green ratings
Top five critical actions with clear implementation guidance
Cyber Risk Snapshot report suitable for leadership review
30-minute walkthrough of findings and recommendations
customerOutcomes: A clear numerical picture of your overall cyber risk in plain English
The five most critical gaps identified so you know where to start
A repeatable baseline for measuring security improvement over time
Risk documentation useful for your first insurance application

full_cybersecurity_assessment.marketingCopy: A comprehensive cybersecurity assessment is the foundation of any serious security program - it's how you move from guessing to knowing. The Full Cybersecurity Assessment methodically reviews your environment across eight or more domains: identity and access, endpoints, email, network, backup and disaster recovery, applications, physical security, and governance. Using recognized frameworks like NIST and CIS Controls as our lens, we interview key people, review actual configurations, and produce a detailed findings report with dozens of risk-rated findings. Each finding includes evidence, why it matters, and estimated remediation effort. You also receive an executive summary built for leadership and board review, plus a phased remediation roadmap with budget-level guidance.
bestFor: Organizations that want a thorough, evidence-based security assessment across all domains
Businesses preparing for compliance audits, certifications, or major security investments
Companies that experienced an incident and need the full risk picture to recover properly
Leadership teams that need defensible evidence to justify security budget
whatIsIncluded: Full-scope assessment across eight or more security domains
Stakeholder interviews with owners, IT contacts, and key staff
Configuration review of accessible systems and platforms
Detailed findings report with risk ratings, evidence, and remediation guidance
Executive summary suitable for board or leadership presentation
Phased remediation roadmap with priorities and estimated effort
Findings walkthrough with Q&A
customerOutcomes: A complete, evidence-based inventory of your security gaps and strengths
Risk-rated findings you can prioritize by actual business impact
Board-ready documentation that turns security into a decision-support function
A phased roadmap that sequences remediation by risk and effort

m365_security_assessment.marketingCopy: Your Microsoft 365 tenant holds your email, files, identities, and collaboration - and its default settings aren't secure enough for most businesses. The M365 Security Assessment is a focused review of everything that matters in your tenant: MFA and Conditional Access, admin role assignments, external sharing and guest access, email protection, retention and backup posture, and identity risk configurations. We inspect the actual settings in your tenant (not a questionnaire), document what's configured versus what Microsoft recommends, and rank every gap by risk so you can fix the dangerous items first. It's the definitive answer to 'how secure is our Microsoft 365, really?'
bestFor: Businesses running Microsoft 365 that haven't had a security review of their tenant
Organizations that inherited a tenant from a previous provider or employee
Companies concerned about external sharing, guest access, or admin sprawl
Businesses preparing for insurance or compliance reviews that cover cloud security
whatIsIncluded: MFA and Conditional Access policy review in your actual tenant
Global and delegated admin role assignment audit
External sharing and guest access review across SharePoint, OneDrive, and Teams
Email protection review covering anti-phishing, anti-spam, and spoofing controls
Retention, backup, and data-loss-prevention posture review
Identity risk configuration review (legacy auth, risky sign-ins, stale accounts)
Risk-ranked findings report with tenant-specific remediation guidance
customerOutcomes: A tenant-specific picture of your M365 security posture with real settings as evidence
The most dangerous gaps (legacy auth, admin sprawl, wide-open external sharing) identified first
Clear, actionable changes mapped to your actual tenant configuration
Insurance-ready documentation of your cloud security controls

small_business_ransomware_readiness_revi.marketingCopy: Ransomware doesn't just hit big companies - small businesses are the favorite target because they're easier and less likely to have tested backups. The Small Business Ransomware Readiness Review checks the specific controls that decide whether you survive an attack or shut down: are your backups real, tested, and off-site; is MFA stopping account takeover; is endpoint protection active; do users have admin rights they shouldn't; and is there a documented recovery path? We assess each control, show you the gaps in plain English, and rank the fixes by how much they improve your odds of a fast recovery. This review focuses on the handful of things that actually determine ransomware outcomes.
bestFor: Businesses worried about ransomware but unsure whether their backups would actually save them
Organizations with backups that have never been tested
Companies where users have local admin rights or MFA isn't enforced
Businesses that want to understand ransomware survival odds before an attack
whatIsIncluded: Backup assessment: does it exist, does it run, is it off-site, and has it been tested
MFA coverage review across email and critical cloud accounts
Endpoint protection and patch posture review
Local admin rights review across workstations
Recovery documentation and incident-response readiness check
Ransomware Readiness Scorecard with prioritized hardening steps
customerOutcomes: A clear answer to 'would we survive ransomware' with evidence for each control
Tested-backup gaps identified before you need the backup
A prioritized hardening list ranked by recovery impact
Documented ransomware readiness for insurance applications

nonprofit_cyber_readiness_review.marketingCopy: Nonprofits, churches, and community organizations handle donor data, member information, and volunteer access - yet they're frequently targeted by cybercriminals who assume they can't afford defenses. The Nonprofit Cyber Readiness Review is a budget-aware cybersecurity assessment designed specifically for mission-driven organizations. We evaluate the essentials that matter most at your size: email security and MFA, backup and recovery, volunteer account management, online giving platforms, and staff security habits. Recommendations are prioritized by cost and impact, with free and low-cost options highlighted first. We understand you can't spend like an enterprise - so we focus on the highest-impact protections that fit a nonprofit budget.
bestFor: Nonprofits, churches, and community organizations with limited IT budgets
Organizations that handle donor, member, or volunteer data
Groups that rely on volunteers who come and go with access to accounts
Nonprofits applying for grants or insurance that require security readiness
whatIsIncluded: Email security and MFA coverage review
Backup and recovery posture assessment
Volunteer account and access management review
Online giving and payment platform security check
Staff security awareness and practice review
Budget-aware recommendations with free and low-cost options prioritized
customerOutcomes: A realistic picture of your organization's security posture with nonprofit constraints in mind
High-impact fixes identified that fit a limited budget
Volunteer access risks documented and addressed
Grant- and insurance-ready evidence of responsible data stewardship

vendor_access_review.marketingCopy: Every vendor with a login into your systems is a potential entry point - and most small businesses have no idea how many vendors have access, to what, or whether that access was ever revoked. The Vendor Access Review maps your vendor relationships to actual system access: who has remote access, which shared accounts exist, what third parties can reach, and what happens to access when a vendor relationship ends. We identify vendor accounts that should have been removed years ago, shared credentials that vendors use that create accountability gaps, and remote-access paths that bypass your security controls. You get a complete vendor-access map and a cleanup plan with documented approvals.
bestFor: Businesses that have worked with multiple vendors, contractors, or IT providers over time
Organizations where vendors use shared or generic accounts
Companies that aren't sure which third parties currently have remote access
Businesses preparing for insurance or compliance reviews covering third-party risk
whatIsIncluded: Complete inventory of vendor accounts and their system access
Shared and generic vendor credential review
Remote access path review (VPN, RDP, remote support tools)
Vendor access offboarding process review
Identification of stale vendor accounts that should be revoked
Vendor Access Map and prioritized cleanup plan
customerOutcomes: A complete map of which vendors can access what - and which shouldn't anymore
Shared vendor credentials documented and remediation path defined
Stale vendor access removed with approved, logged changes
Third-party risk evidence ready for insurance and compliance reviews

admin_privilege_review.marketingCopy: Admin privileges are the crown jewels of your IT environment - and the accounts that hold them are what attackers target first. The Admin Privilege Review digs into every high-privilege account in your business: who has administrator rights in Microsoft 365, on servers, on domain controllers, and on business-critical cloud apps. We check role assignments against actual job needs, flag excessive or inherited permissions, identify break-glass and shared admin accounts, and assess how changes to privileged access are approved and tracked. You end up with a documented picture of who can do what at the highest levels - and a plan to move toward least privilege without breaking daily operations.
bestFor: Organizations with multiple admins, past IT providers, or unclear role assignments
Businesses that have given out admin rights casually over the years
Companies that don't have a documented map of who holds elevated access
Organizations preparing for audits, insurance, or compliance reviews
whatIsIncluded: High-privilege account inventory across Microsoft 365, servers, and cloud apps
Role assignment review against actual job responsibilities
Excessive, stale, and shared privileged account identification
Break-glass and emergency access account review
Privileged access change-management process assessment
Least-privilege remediation roadmap with documented approvals
customerOutcomes: A complete map of every account with elevated access and why it has it
Excessive or unnecessary admin rights identified and removed with approval
Reduced attack surface where compromise of one account no longer means full control
Privileged access evidence ready for audit and insurance review

mfa_enforcement_project.marketingCopy: Enabling MFA on one account is easy; enforcing it across every user and system without locking anyone out is a project. The MFA Enforcement Project plans and implements a broader MFA rollout across the systems that matter to your business. We start with a coverage assessment, then build a rollout plan that includes Microsoft 365 Conditional Access enforcement, onboarding of every user with clear instructions, and coverage of critical third-party platforms like banking, payroll, and your domain registrar. We handle the coordination, the enrollment support, and the verification - so MFA gets turned on everywhere, staff stay productive, and nobody gets stuck. When the project is done, MFA isn't optional anymore; it's the rule.
bestFor: Businesses ready to enforce MFA everywhere but worried about rollout friction
Organizations with partial MFA coverage and no clear path to full enforcement
Companies where MFA is 'suggested' but not required across all users
Businesses whose insurance or compliance requirements mandate full MFA enforcement
whatIsIncluded: MFA coverage assessment across all business systems
Microsoft 365 Conditional Access policy design and enforcement
User enrollment plan with step-by-step instructions for every staff member
MFA enablement for critical third-party platforms
Enrollment support and lockout prevention planning
Post-rollout verification that MFA applies to all users and admin actions
customerOutcomes: MFA enforced as a requirement rather than a suggestion across your environment
Every user enrolled and comfortable with their authenticator setup
Critical third-party accounts protected by a second factor
Audit-ready evidence that MFA covers your business

password_manager_rollout.marketingCopy: A password manager is the single most practical tool for eliminating weak and reused passwords - but only if it's deployed properly and people actually use it. The Password Manager Rollout goes beyond installing software: we help you select the right platform for your team (Bitwarden, 1Password, or Keeper), configure the organization with shared vaults and permissions, migrate critical credentials from spreadsheets and browsers, and train every user on day-to-day use. Staff stop reusing passwords, shared accounts get controlled by the business instead of shared in a spreadsheet, and you get visibility into credential hygiene that didn't exist before. It's the password hygiene project, done so it sticks.
bestFor: Businesses ready to move off spreadsheets and browser-saved passwords
Organizations that want shared team credentials without insecure sharing
Companies that bought a password manager but never actually deployed it properly
Businesses that want to eliminate password reuse as a practical security improvement
whatIsIncluded: Password manager platform selection and comparison tailored to your team
Organization setup with shared vaults, folders, and permission structure
Migration of critical credentials from spreadsheets and browsers
Browser and device extension rollout for all users
Staff training on password generation, sharing, and daily use
Admin guidance for ongoing vault management and access reviews
customerOutcomes: A deployed, configured password manager that staff actually use daily
Shared credentials controlled by the business instead of shared informally
Elimination of password reuse across the most important accounts
Visible credential hygiene that improves your security posture and audit story

email_security_hardening.marketingCopy: Email is the attack surface attackers exploit most - through spoofed domains, phishing, and misconfigured authentication. The Email Security Hardening service configures practical, high-impact email protections rather than just reviewing them. We correct your SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records so your domain can't be easily impersonated, tighten Microsoft 365 anti-phishing and anti-spam policies including impersonation protection, review mailbox rules for compromise indicators, and confirm MFA protects every mailbox. We make the changes that meaningfully reduce phishing and business email compromise, verify delivery still works, and document what we configured. It's email security turned from a recommendation into a completed configuration.
bestFor: Businesses that want email protections actually configured, not just reviewed
Organizations whose domain is being spoofed or whose email lands in spam
Companies with Microsoft 365 that never customized anti-phishing settings
Businesses hardening their email before insurance or compliance review
whatIsIncluded: SPF, DKIM, and DMARC correction and verification
Microsoft 365 anti-phishing policy configuration including impersonation protection
Anti-spam and quarantine settings tuning
Mailbox rule audit for compromise indicators
MFA verification on all mailboxes
Post-change deliverability testing and documentation
customerOutcomes: A domain that attackers can't easily impersonate in email
Hardened Microsoft 365 policies that filter more phishing before it reaches inboxes
Compromise indicators like suspicious forwarding rules identified and removed
Documented email security configuration you can show insurers and auditors

endpoint_protection_rollout.marketingCopy: Endpoint protection is only effective if it's deployed on every device, configured properly, and actually being monitored. The Endpoint Protection Rollout ensures your business computers - Windows and Mac - are running a real, current, centrally managed endpoint security solution. We assess what's currently on each device (including the dangerous state of 'nothing' or expired consumer antivirus), select an appropriate business solution, deploy it across your fleet, configure detection and response settings, and set up a monitoring process so alerts aren't ignored. Your endpoints stop being the soft target attackers rely on and start being defended, managed, and accounted for.
bestFor: Businesses with a mix of unprotected or inconsistently protected devices
Organizations relying on free or expired consumer antivirus
Companies that want centrally managed endpoint security across their fleet
Businesses preparing for insurance that requires endpoint protection
whatIsIncluded: Current endpoint protection state assessment across all devices
Solution selection and licensing guidance (Microsoft Defender for Business or similar)
Central deployment across Windows and Mac workstations
Detection, response, and alert configuration
Monitoring process setup so security events aren't missed
Deployment documentation and fleet-wide coverage verification
customerOutcomes: Every business device running current, managed endpoint protection
A centrally managed view of your fleet's security status
Detection and response that flags real threats instead of silent gaps
Insurance- and audit-ready endpoint coverage evidence

local_admin_removal_project.marketingCopy: When every user has local administrator rights on their computer, a single click on a malicious file can take down the whole machine - and your data. The Local Admin Removal Project reduces these privileges across your selected workstations without disrupting productivity. We identify which users actually need admin rights, plan the removal so legitimate software installs still work, execute the change across the fleet, and handle the support tickets that follow so the transition doesn't break your staff. Removing local admin is one of the most effective, least expensive hardening measures available - and doing it as a planned project instead of a surprise is the only way it succeeds.
bestFor: Businesses where every user can install software and change system settings
Organizations that want a high-impact hardening win with minimal disruption
Companies that have dealt with malware infections that started with local admin
Businesses preparing for insurance or compliance that limits admin rights
whatIsIncluded: Current local admin rights assessment across selected workstations
Legitimate software install and update needs analysis
Local admin removal plan with exception management
Fleet-wide execution of the privilege change
Post-change support for staff affected by the transition
Documentation of who retains admin rights and why
customerOutcomes: Local admin privileges removed across the fleet, shrinking the malware blast radius
Legitimate software installs still working through approved processes
A managed exception list instead of everyone-has-admin by default
A documented hardening improvement that insurers and auditors recognize

bitlocker_encryption_rollout.marketingCopy: A stolen or lost laptop containing customer data is a breach - unless the drive is encrypted. The BitLocker Encryption Rollout enables full-disk encryption on your supported business devices so that if a computer is lost or stolen, the data on it is unreadable. We verify which devices support BitLocker (and review Mac equivalents), enable encryption properly with recovery keys stored somewhere safe, confirm it's actually protecting data rather than just enabled, and document the recovery key locations so you never get locked out of your own data. Disk encryption is a core insurance and compliance requirement, and this rollout makes it a configured, verified reality.
bestFor: Businesses with laptops that travel, remote workers, or field staff
Organizations that handle customer, payment, or health data on portable devices
Companies that aren't sure whether their drives are actually encrypted
Businesses meeting insurance or compliance requirements for data-at-rest protection
whatIsIncluded: BitLocker support and readiness assessment across business devices
Full-disk encryption enablement with verified protection status
Recovery key collection and secure storage
Mac drive encryption review (FileVault) where applicable
TPM configuration and compatibility handling
Encryption status documentation for all devices
customerOutcomes: Every eligible business device with verified full-disk encryption
Recovery keys safely stored so encryption never becomes a lockout
Lost or stolen devices no longer exposing business data
Data-at-rest protection evidence for insurance and compliance

dns_filtering_setup.marketingCopy: DNS filtering blocks dangerous websites before your users even reach them, catching phishing, malware, and ransomware delivery at the network level. The DNS Filtering Setup configures protective DNS for your business where it's appropriate, creating a first line of defense that works even when users click something they shouldn't. We evaluate your current DNS setup, recommend an appropriate filtering service, configure it so business traffic is protected while web browsing stays functional, and handle exception requests so legitimate sites aren't blocked. DNS filtering is invisible to your staff but actively blocking threats every day - one of the highest-value, lowest-friction security controls available.
bestFor: Businesses that want network-level protection beyond endpoint software
Organizations that want to block known-malicious sites without blocking productivity
Companies preparing for insurance that rewards layered security controls
Businesses that want an always-on safety net for click-prone staff
whatIsIncluded: Current DNS configuration and security review
Protective DNS service selection (e.g., Cisco Umbrella, DNSFilter, or similar)
Configuration so all business traffic resolves through filtered DNS
Category and policy configuration to balance security with productivity
Exception handling for legitimate blocked sites
Documentation and verification that filtering is active
customerOutcomes: Network-level blocking of known phishing, malware, and ransomware domains
Protection that works even when a user clicks a bad link
A filtered DNS environment that doesn't break legitimate browsing
Another layered control documented for insurance and compliance

security_awareness_training_setup.marketingCopy: Your staff are the ones who see phishing emails first - and trained staff are your cheapest, most effective security control. The Security Awareness Training Setup establishes a real, ongoing training workflow rather than a one-time lecture. We help you select a training platform that fits your size (KnowBe4, PhishLabs, or similar), configure automated training campaigns, set up phishing simulation schedules, and establish how results get reviewed and reported. You get a system that trains staff continuously, measures who's clicking, and produces the awareness data cyber insurers increasingly require. It's security training that runs itself month after month.
bestFor: Businesses that want ongoing training rather than an annual one-off
Organizations that need phishing simulation data for insurance
Companies with staff who regularly click on suspicious emails
Businesses that want a measurable awareness program without running it manually

Platform configuration with automated training campaigns
Phishing simulation schedule and content setup
User enrollment and role assignment
Result review and reporting process establishment

customerOutcomes: Continuous security training that reaches every staff member automatically
Real phishing click and report data to drive improvements
Insurance-ready awareness program evidence
A self-running program your business can sustain without daily effort

incident_response_plan_starter.marketingCopy: The organizations that recover fastest from security incidents are the ones that already decided what to do before the incident happened. The Incident Response Plan Starter creates a practical, first-response plan tailored to your business - not a generic template. We define escalation triggers, assign roles and responsibilities, document the exact steps to contain common incidents like email compromise, ransomware, and data breaches, and establish communication procedures with staff, customers, insurers, and authorities. We keep it actionable: your team knows who's in charge, what to touch, what not to touch, and who to call. It's the difference between a controlled response and a panic.
bestFor: Businesses with no incident response documentation at all
Organizations that want a usable plan instead of a theoretical policy
Companies whose insurance or compliance requires an incident response plan
Small teams that need clear roles and escalation steps defined in advance

cyber_insurance_readiness_package.marketingCopy: Cyber insurance applications are increasingly strict - and many small businesses get denied, quoted higher premiums, or hit with coverage carve-outs because of common gaps like missing MFA, untested backups, or no documented policies. The Cyber Insurance Readiness Package gets your business in a defensible position before you apply. We review the controls insurers commonly require (MFA, backup, endpoint protection, admin access, incident response, training), help you address the gaps within scope, and compile the evidence insurers ask for. You approach the application with documentation instead of hoping, which improves approval odds, premium levels, and coverage terms.
bestFor: Businesses applying for cyber insurance and unsure what the questionnaire means
Organizations that were denied coverage or quoted high premiums due to gaps
Companies that want to strengthen controls before their renewal
Businesses that want a documented readiness posture rather than best-effort answers

Better approval odds and, in many cases, better premiums and coverage terms

security_awareness_lunch_learn.marketingCopy: A one-hour lunch-and-learn is one of the most cost-effective security investments a small business can make - because your staff are the first line of defense. The Security Awareness Lunch & Learn delivers a practical, engaging training session on phishing, passwords, MFA, and safe everyday habits, customized to your team and the threats they actually face. We use real-world examples and interactive discussion rather than slides nobody remembers, and every attendee leaves with a cheat sheet they can actually use. It's perfect for kicking off a security culture or refreshing staff who've become complacent.

Organizations that haven't done any security training and want to start
Companies with staff who've fallen for phishing or weak-password habits
Teams that need a refresher that's engaging rather than boring

owner_admin_security_training.marketingCopy: Owners and administrators hold the keys to your business - and their accounts are the highest-value targets. The Owner/Admin Security Training is focused, technical security training for the people who manage your systems: the business owner, the office manager who handles admin accounts, and anyone with elevated access. We cover the specific attacks aimed at privileged users (phishing targeting admins, password attacks, session theft), how to protect admin accounts with MFA and least privilege, how to review security alerts and audit logs, and how to handle a suspected compromise. This is training for the people whose compromise would be catastrophic - so they stop being the weakest link.
bestFor: Business owners who personally hold admin accounts
Office managers or staff who administer email, domains, and cloud apps
Organizations where one person's compromise would be catastrophic
Businesses that want their privileged users to know how to spot admin-targeted attacks

customerOutcomes: Privileged users who recognize attacks aimed specifically at them
Protected admin accounts with MFA and least-privilege habits

staff_security_starter.marketingCopy: New and existing staff need the security basics before they become a risk - and most small businesses have no formal way to teach them. The Staff Security Starter delivers a packaged set of security training and reference materials that equips every employee with the essentials: recognizing phishing, creating strong passwords, using MFA, handling sensitive data, and knowing what to do if something looks wrong. We customize the materials to your business, provide printable cheat sheets and quick-reference guides, and structure it so new hires can be onboarded quickly and existing staff can refresh easily. It's a security baseline that scales with every person you hire.
bestFor: Businesses that want a repeatable security onboarding process for staff
Organizations that have never provided formal security guidance to employees
Companies with high turnover that onboard new staff frequently
Businesses that want consistent security expectations across the team
